## Known biases

- **Startup mismatch.** The V4 9-bar case has long-time flow 1.86 against 1.82 g/s and reaches 36 g at ×0.65 of the measured time. The model's flow reaches 90% of its 100 s value 13.6 s after the first drops instead of 25.5 s, and its first drops come 6.28 s after full pressure instead of 12.8 s. The held-out V3 and V5 time ratios are ×0.81 and ×0.78. Total shot times combine startup and permeability errors; they do not isolate κ_ref.
- **Pump saturation in V1.** 15 of 15 Schmieder shots reach the pump's 12 bar limit during the preinfusion-to-pour switch (for 2.7–4 s); the pours of experiment(s) 2, 12, 13 reach the limit (longest 0.6 s). The measured per-shot maxima are 2.5–9.3 bar (Table S3). The simplified DE1 control and startup hydraulics do not reproduce those maxima.
- **κ_ref rests on structural choices.** ×2.3 across the four estimates (the two datasets ×2.2); ×4.7 between the whole-shot and pour-phase pressure comparisons; ×1.9 between θ = 0 and θ = 0.27. Fit uncertainties describe the chosen model and do not include this structural spread.
- **Local uncertainties omit model discrepancy.** Reduced chi-square 3.6 (χ²/n by block: V1 3.04, V2 5.15, V4 12.3, V6 2.85); V1 holds 315 of 339 residuals, and its cup masses share information with c₀, λ and the first fraction (Eq. 3).
- **EY levels.** V3 and V5 EY rest on the bean's 28% extractable solids (input models), which no M1 dataset calibrates for those coffees.
- **V2.** The model's Bodenstein number is above the data in 4 of 5 cases; the held-out compound curves were not run (licence).

Datasets, case builders and the calibration harness: [case-builders.md](case-builders.md),
[calibration.md](calibration.md). Targets: [PLAN §10](../PLAN.md#10-verification-and-validation).

### Registry-value pruning review

A weak local marginal SD nominates a parameter for a bounded refit at its registry value. Removal requires a successful, finite refit without unavailable final predictions and training cost no more than 1% above both the initial pre-prune fit (cost 569.569) and the preceding accepted fit. This is an operational tolerance, not a significance or confidence threshold. Retained candidates can depend on bounds and coupled model assumptions; their retention does not establish independent identification. Rejected trials do not replace the accepted fit.

**Reference permeability** `hydraulics.permeability.reference`: pooled 1.49e-13 m² (geometric mean over datasets, each dataset the geometric mean of its estimates; estimate i = fitted bare κ₀,i / builder scaling of case i, (D32_i/D32_ref)²·KC(ε)/KC(ε_ref)). By dataset: schmieder2023 1.02e-13 m²; waszkiewicz2026 2.19e-13 m²; the datasets differ by ×2.16, more than their fit uncertainties: the pooled value carries that disagreement. Spread of all estimates: log-SD 0.39, max/min 2.29.

Each estimate is the fitted bare κ₀ divided by the builder's scaling of the app's representation of that grind (the scaling basis). D32 values from different bases are not strictly comparable: Waszkiewicz's PSD is laser diffraction (Mastersizer 2000; the article does not say wet or dry dispersion), while the grinder presets' D32 comes from the input models, anchored on other measurements.

| Nuisance κ₀ | Dataset | Scaling basis | κ₀ (m²) | Builder scaling | D32/D32_ref | κ_ref (m²) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `calibration.schmieder2023.permeability.gl1_7` | schmieder2023 | grinder preset mahlkoenig-e65s at GL 1.7 | 4.26e-14 | 0.445 | 0.667 | 9.59e-14 |
| `calibration.schmieder2023.permeability.gl2_0` | schmieder2023 | grinder preset mahlkoenig-e65s at GL 2.0 | 5.29e-14 | 0.48 | 0.692 | 1.1e-13 |
| `calibration.waszkiewicz2026.permeability` | waszkiewicz2026 | the case's own PSD | 1.92e-14 | 0.0877 | 0.296 | 2.19e-13 |

**Tension with typical espresso grinds.** Published espresso grinds have a dry D32 of about 80–145 µm (Cameron, Corrochano ΨB–E, Smrke), while Waszkiewicz's grind measures about 49 µm (it was chosen for the SCA guideline of 37 g in 32 s at 9 bar; the article's own 9 bar shots reached 37 g at about 48 s). κ₀ scales with D32², so differences in the measured PSD affect the reference permeability inferred from each dataset. The held-out shot times come out at ×0.81 (V3 Cameron, mean error -6.1 s) and ×0.78 (V5 Smrke, -13 s). The V4 case, calibrated on long-time flow, reaches 36 g at ×0.65 of its measured time. These times combine startup and permeability effects. κ_ref is not tuned to them.

- *Waszkiewicz's PSD is atypical.* X50 61 µm, X90 145 µm, 63.6% of the volume below 100 µm; 3.8% of the volume sits in the 158–182 µm bin and nothing above, although the bins run to 417 µm and the Mastersizer 2000 reads to 2000 µm. A coarse tail that ends this abruptly suggests that coarse particles were under-represented (settling in a wet dispersion unit, or sample selection; the article does not say), which lowers this D32 and raises this dataset's κ_ref. The authors describe their grounds as "of typical size below 200 µm".
- *Schmieder's reference-permeability scaling uses the E65S dial mapping.* The dial's scale is disputed (the brochure's ≈5 µm per indicator read as burr movement or as a particle-size bandwidth), so the preset maps the dial to a burr gap fitted to the article's wet-laser D[4,3] at GL 1.4 and 2.0, and its D32 comes from the input models' fines relation (fitted to dry-laser and Camsizer PSDs), not from the article's wet D32 of 27–29 µm, which includes 1–10 µm debris. A 10% smaller scaling-basis D32 with fitted κ₀ and reference D32 held fixed would raise the Schmieder κ_ref estimate by about 23%.

**V1 particle input in this run:** the qualified Schmieder Fig. A1b wet CDF, with its unresolved fine tail constrained by the published D32. The E65S D32 above is only the reference-permeability scaling basis; it is not the PSD simulated in these V1 cases. D32 agreement is an input constraint, and wet-dispersed debris is not independently validated as dry-puck geometry or a particle diffusion length. The dataset sidecar's note about the historical default describes the 0.5.1 input audit; this run's explicit calibration configuration selects the wet CDF.

The wet-PSD rows reconstruct the unresolved finest-particle head with the published D32 shifted by ±1 SD, leaving the resolved tail CDF and parameter priors unchanged. They are input sensitivities followed by refitting, not confidence bands or additional independent observations. Each reconstruction changes the particle sizes supplied to the model, including its derived pore-air timescale.

### Structural sensitivity: dissolution share θ

A sensitivity analysis of a structural assumption, not a choice: the calibration fixes θ at its mechanistic default, 0 (the insoluble cell walls hold the particle envelope, so dissolution opens intraparticle pores). θ is collinear with the bed permeability: the grinding-level permeabilities and contents move to absorb it, so κ₀ and κ_ref change with it. The row refits V1+V2+V4+V6 at the old value: total cost 641.7 against 704.8 at θ = 0, peak-pressure RMS 1.79; 1 of 15 V1 pours sit at the pump's 12 bar limit. A degenerate refit like this is not evidence for or against θ. Independent evidence for θ would have to come from flow-rise data, which M1 holds out (V4 transient), or from new experiments. The rows repeat the held-out predictions at both values.

| θ | κ₀: Schmieder GL 1.4, 1.7, 2.0; Waszkiewicz (m²) | κ_ref by dataset (m²) | pooled κ_ref (m²) | V3 time model/data | V3 peak EY | V5 time model/data | V5 mean EY | V5 ρ(time, EY) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (calibration) | 4.09e-14, 4.26e-14, 5.29e-14, 1.92e-14 | schmieder2023 1.02e-13, waszkiewicz2026 2.19e-13 | 1.49e-13 | ×0.81 | 19.4% at GS 1.1 | ×0.78 | 18.3% | 0.84 |
| 0.27 (old proportional rule; pump-capped) | 3.16e-14, 3.23e-14, 3.92e-14, 6.89e-15 | schmieder2023 7.69e-14, waszkiewicz2026 7.86e-14 | 7.78e-14 | ×0.88 | 16.8% at GS 1.1 | ×0.85 | 16.5% | 0.65 |
